T: Two rats. One city. Plenty of chowder.
D: A cop goes undercover with Boston's Irish mob while a mob mole rises in the police.
P: Serve the mains when Costigan and Sullivan figure out who the other one is.
S: with oyster crackers, the Boston way
Render bacon, sweat onion and celery, add diced potato, clam juice and thyme, simmer, add chopped clams and cream for the last 3 minutes. Oyster crackers.
Wholemeal flour, bicarb, salt and buttermilk mixed into a soft round, cut with a deep cross, baked at 220C for 35 minutes, thick slices with salted butter.
Clam meat soaked in evaporated milk, dredged in corn flour and plain flour, fried at 185C for 60 seconds. Tartare and lemon.
M: the Irish pub where the crew drinks
Flathead or cod dipped in a batter of flour, cornflour and ice-cold lager, fried at 180C. Triple-cooked chips, mushy peas with mint, malt vinegar.
Cooked lobster tossed lightly with mayo, lemon and celery, piled into butter-toasted split-top rolls, chives.
W: Two genoise layers sandwiched with vanilla crème pâtissière, glossy dark chocolate ganache poured over the top.
K: Costigan's bar order, a natural diuretic, and the bartender's remark

Cranberry juice shaken with fresh lime and a little orange, topped with soda over crushed ice, vodka optional if you need to keep your cover. Shake 400ml cranberry juice, 60ml lime juice, 60ml orange juice and 20ml sugar syrup with ice for 10 seconds. Strain into 4 short glasses filled with crushed ice. Top each with 50ml soda water and add a lime wedge. For the grown-up version, add 30ml vodka to each glass before topping.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 2 days, keep chilled; reheat gently

steps.text: Dice the bacon, onion, celery and potatoes.
Fry the bacon until crisp, then sweat the onion and celery in the fat until soft.
Add the potatoes, clam juice and thyme and simmer until the potato is tender.
Stir in the clam meat and cream and warm through. Serve in cups with oyster crackers.

dishes.make_ahead: Best the day it is baked

steps.text: Mix the flours, bicarb and salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Shape into a round and cut a deep cross on top.
Bake at 220C until golden and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Rest the loaf, then slice thick and serve with the salted butter.
Cut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry well. Whisk the batter flour, cornflour and cold lager together.
Fry the chips in oil at 140C until pale and soft, then drain.
Cook the peas, then crush with the butter and chopped mint and keep warm.
Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180C in batches until golden and crisp.
Fry the chips again at 185C until crisp. Salt well and serve with the fish, peas and malt vinegar.
Whisk 4 of the eggs with half the sugar until thick and pale. Fold in the flour and divide between two lined 20cm tins.
Bake at 180C until springy, then turn out and cool completely.
Heat the milk. Whisk 3 yolks with the remaining sugar and cornflour, whisk in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir until thick.
Chill the custard until cold and set.
Sandwich the sponges with custard. Melt the chocolate with the cream and pour over the top.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix the base up to 1 day ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Shake the cranberry juice, lime juice, orange juice and syrup with ice, then strain into 4 short glasses of crushed ice. Top with soda and a lime wedge. Add vodka first for the grown-up version.

s.note: Creamy clam and potato chowder with bacon and oyster crackers.
s.how: Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp, then sweat 1 diced onion and 2 celery sticks in the fat. Add 400g diced potatoes, 500ml clam juice or fish stock and thyme and simmer 15 minutes. Stir in 250g chopped clam meat and 200ml cream for the last 3 minutes. Serve in cups with 100g oyster crackers.

s.note: Quick Irish soda bread, warm, thick with salted butter.
s.how: Mix 250g wholemeal flour, 250g plain flour, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 1 tsp salt. Stir in 450ml buttermilk to a soft dough, shape into a round, cut a deep cross on top and bake at 220C for 35 minutes until it sounds hollow. Rest 10 minutes, slice thick and serve with 100g salted butter.

m.note: Lager-battered flathead with chips, minted mushy peas and malt vinegar.
m.how: Whisk 200g plain flour, 50g cornflour and 330ml ice-cold lager into a batter. Dust 800g flathead fillets in flour, dip and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Fry 1kg potatoes as chips at 140C then 185C. Cook 400g frozen peas, crush with butter and mint. Serve with malt vinegar.

w.note: Two sponge layers filled with vanilla custard under dark chocolate ganache.
w.how: Whisk 4 eggs and 120g sugar until thick, fold in 120g flour and bake in two 20cm tins at 180C for 18 minutes. For custard, heat 300ml milk, whisk into 3 yolks, 60g sugar and 25g cornflour and cook until thick, then cool. Sandwich the sponges with custard. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream and pour over the top.
